gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The assistant ___ I spoke to was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after a preposition-style clause.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The exam, the results of ___ will be published on Friday, was very difficult.
gaps.hint: quantity noun + of + thing in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'The results of which' joins the clauses formally; 'of whom' is for people and 'of them' cannot link clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: That's exactly ___ I needed — thank you!
gaps.explanation: 'What I needed' means 'the thing that I needed'; 'that' cannot be used in this free relative position.

gaps.sentence: Tell me ___ you said to her.
gaps.explanation: 'What you said' means 'the words that you said'; 'that' cannot head the clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up today.
gaps.explanation: 'Anyone who' is the standard pattern; 'who' is the subject pronoun for people.
